newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki falls across board, U.S. jitters continue.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki falls across board, U.S. jitters continue.

text.p: Shares fell across the board on Thursday for the second day after setting records on Tuesday, with continued Wall Street jitters and a downward correction in the dollar hitting Nokia and forestries, brokers said.
The HEX general index fell almost percent to close at 2,946.63 points and the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark closed down 1.07 percent at 1,028.27 points.
Wall Street stocks fell at the open on Thursday, undermined by a weak bond market following data which was seen as strengthening the argument for Fed tightening.
"The jitters will continue," one broker said, adding that the U.S. and other markets were now waiting for the Fed's FOMC meeting on March 25 for new interest rate views.
"Fundamentals are not behind this. This is a sentiment game," said another one broker.
Paper machine maker Valmet was the second most traded -- over 100 million markka volume -- with heavy selling pressure brining it down over two percent to 87.10 markka.
"A big owner wanted to get quickly out of Valmet, but buyers were also found for the stock," one broker said. "It's foreign investors on the selling side," said another.
